name: EU AI Act
description: Lax tier — bare minimum critical security for AI workloads. Citations are at article granularity only; the paragraph actually engaged, and every check that is a proxy rather than evidence, is named in each control set's description and in the citation table in ../README.md. Verified against CELEX 32024R1689. UNPRICED: every check in this version declares freqTriple {min: 0, mode: 0, max: 0}, so fair.Simulate returns zero and a failing check contributes GBP 0.00 of annual loss. The riskTriple states loss magnitude only; loss-event frequency has never been calibrated for this tier. A scan of this version reports zero total exposure however many controls fail. The zeros are declared rather than omitted so the absence of pricing is visible in the pack instead of arriving as a Go zero value. Do not quote a figure from this version. v2.1 carries real frequency triples. See ../README.md, section 'Pricing'.

controlSets.name: Art. 9(2)(d) — Risk Management Measures
controlSets.description: Article 9 requires a risk management system; 9(2)(d) requires 'the adoption of appropriate and targeted risk management measures'. It names no technical control, so every check in this set is a proxy for a documented measure. Container hardening is more directly an Article 15(5) cybersecurity measure, and a liveness probe is more directly an Article 15(4) resilience measure.

controls.name: AI containers run as non-root
controls.description: High-risk AI systems must not run with root privileges

checks.name: Container runs as non-root
checks.description: No container may run as UID 0. An explicit runAsNonRoot: false or runAsUser: 0 is fatal at pod level and at container level; otherwise a container without its own runAsNonRoot inherits the pod value. Pod Security Admission restricted rejects a pod that sets runAsNonRoot: false at pod level even where every container overrides it to true, so a pass here means the pod is admissible, not merely that it would run non-root.
checks.celExpression: has(object.spec) && has(object.spec.containers) && size(object.spec.containers) > 0 && !(has(object.spec.securityContext) && has(object.spec.securityContext.runAsUser) && object.spec.securityContext.runAsUser == 0) && !(has(object.spec.securityContext) && has(object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot) && object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == false) && (object.spec.containers + (has(object.spec.initContainers) ? object.spec.initContainers : []) + (has(object.spec.ephemeralContainers) ? object.spec.ephemeralContainers : [])).all(c, ((has(c.securityContext) && has(c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot)) ? c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == true : (has(object.spec.securityContext) && has(object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot) && object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == true)) && !(has(c.securityContext) && has(c.securityContext.runAsUser) && c.securityContext.runAsUser == 0) && !(has(c.securityContext) && has(c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot) && c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == false))

controls.name: No privilege escalation
controls.description: AI containers must not allow privilege escalation

checks.name: Privilege escalation disabled
checks.description: Every container, init container and ephemeral container must set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false. Windows pods are exempt, as they are under Pod Security Admission: the field is a Linux-only field and a Windows pod cannot set it, so demanding it would make a conformant Windows workload impossible to satisfy.
checks.celExpression: has(object.spec) && has(object.spec.containers) && size(object.spec.containers) > 0 && ((has(object.spec.os) && has(object.spec.os.name) && object.spec.os.name == 'windows') || (object.spec.containers + (has(object.spec.initContainers) ? object.spec.initContainers : []) + (has(object.spec.ephemeralContainers) ? object.spec.ephemeralContainers : [])).all(c, has(c.securityContext) && has(c.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation) && c.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == false))

controls.name: No privileged containers
controls.description: AI containers must not run in privileged mode

checks.name: Privileged mode disabled
checks.celExpression: has(object.spec) && has(object.spec.containers) && size(object.spec.containers) > 0 && (object.spec.containers + (has(object.spec.initContainers) ? object.spec.initContainers : []) + (has(object.spec.ephemeralContainers) ? object.spec.ephemeralContainers : [])).all(c, !(has(c.securityContext) && has(c.securityContext.privileged) && c.securityContext.privileged == true))

controlSets.name: Art. 10 — Data and Data Governance
controlSets.description: Article 10 governs the quality and governance of TRAINING, VALIDATION and TESTING data sets (10(2)(a)-(h)). It does not regulate runtime handling or retention of operational data. `data-classification-label` is a weak proxy for 10(2)(a)/(e). `pii-handling-annotation` is MIS-ATTRIBUTED: Article 10's only personal-data provision is 10(5), which permits processing special categories strictly for bias detection and correction; runtime PII handling is a GDPR obligation. `data-retention-annotation` is MIS-ATTRIBUTED: Article 10 imposes no retention period (10(5)(e) requires deletion of special-category bias data only); log retention of at least six months is Article 26(6) and QMS data retention is Article 17(1)(f).

controls.name: Data classification label present
controls.description: Workloads handling training data must declare classification

controlSets.name: Art. 14 — Human Oversight
controlSets.description: Verified. Article 14(4)(d)-(e) requires that the oversight person be enabled to disregard, override or reverse the output and to interrupt the system, and 14(3)(b) allows measures the deployer implements. A declared oversight label, approval gate and override contact are declarations that such measures exist, not evidence of them.

controls.name: Human-in-the-loop label present
controls.description: AI workloads must declare their human oversight level

controlSets.name: Art. 15(4) — Robustness and Resilience
controlSets.description: Verified against Article 15(4): resilience 'regarding errors, faults or inconsistencies', achievable 'through technical redundancy solutions, which may include backup or fail-safe plans'. Resource bounds, probes and a replica floor are redundancy and fail-safe measures. Note that CYBERSECURITY is Article 15(5), not 15(4); no check in this set evidences 15(5).

controls.name: Resource limits defined
controls.description: AI workloads must have resource limits to prevent resource exhaustion

checks.name: CPU and memory limits defined
checks.description: Every container and init container must bound both cpu and memory in resources.limits. Ephemeral containers are excluded: the Kubernetes EphemeralContainer schema forbids resources on them.
checks.celExpression: has(object.spec) && has(object.spec.containers) && size(object.spec.containers) > 0 && (object.spec.containers + (has(object.spec.initContainers) ? object.spec.initContainers : [])).all(c, has(c.resources) && has(c.resources.limits) && 'cpu' in c.resources.limits && 'memory' in c.resources.limits)

controlSets.name: Art. 17(1) — Quality Management System
controlSets.description: Article 17(1) requires a documented quality management system; 17(1)(a) covers 'procedures for the management of modifications' and 17(1)(e) 'technical specifications ... to be applied'. Digest pinning, a trusted-registry allow-list and a policy-version label are proxies for those procedures: a pod spec cannot evidence that a QMS exists. Supply-chain integrity is also engaged by Article 15(5), which names 'pre-trained components used in training (model poisoning)'.

controls.name: Image pinned by digest
controls.description: Container images must use digest references for reproducibility

checks.name: Image uses sha256 digest
checks.celExpression: has(object.spec) && has(object.spec.containers) && size(object.spec.containers) > 0 && (object.spec.containers + (has(object.spec.initContainers) ? object.spec.initContainers : []) + (has(object.spec.ephemeralContainers) ? object.spec.ephemeralContainers : [])).all(c, has(c.image) && c.image.matches('@sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$'))
